page.layout: Running head at top centre (faint). Full-width dedication address in large capitals and roman type, followed by the author's name centred in spaced capitals. Below them one column of body text in roman and italic, with a historiated initial "D" at the start. No marginal notes. A gathering signature at the lower left of the text block.

main_text.head: CLARISSIMIS ET amplissimis viris, & Magnificis Dominis, Dominis suis Syndicis, Senatuíque inclytæ vrbis Geneuæ,
LAMB. DANAEVS.
main_text.p: DVAE sunt potissimùm causæ, Magnifici Domini, quæme-cur has meas in Augustinum commentationes vobis dedicarem, impulerunt : vestrorum erga me beneficiorum recordatio, atque vtilissimum ipsius libri argumentum. Nam quum anteactæ vitæ meæ rationem ineo, & mecum, sicuti par est, expendo, qua via Domino Patri misericordiarum placuerit me primùm ex illis horrendis idololatriæ tenebris ad salutarem Euangelij sui lucem traducere, plurimùm me vobis, ac quantùm neq; parentibus quidem ipsis debere ingenuè profiteor. Quanquam enim parentum in liberos beneficium est omnino ingens, & quantum à liberis nunquam satis pro dignitatē vel agnosci, vel

page.notes: Dropped capital D in the woodcut initial: "D" is the historiated initial, joined to "VAE" as "DVAE". Hyphen-like curved signs after "quæme", "in" and "dignitatē" and "neq;" are doubtful: "quæme-cur" and "neq;" are my best reading of the printed signs. A small mark on the right margin near the middle of the page (about y 1435) is a printer's mark or stain, not text. The page ends mid-sentence ("vel"), with the sentence continuing on the next page. No page number printed. The running head at the top is faint and its reading "EPISTOLA" is uncertain.
